title.zh: 卷二百八十三 列傳第四十二 王欽若 林特 丁謂 夏竦
title.en: Volume 283 Biographies 42: Wang Qinruo, Lin Te, Ding Wei, Xia Song
title.raw: 卷二百八十三 列傳第四十二 王欽若 林特 丁謂 夏竦 Volume 283 Biographies 42: Wang Qinruo, Lin Te, Ding Wei, Xia Song

sentences.zh: 王欽若

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo

sentences.zh: 王欽若，字定國，臨江軍新喻人。

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo, styled Dingguo, was a native of Xinyu in Linjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo, courtesy name Dingguo, came from Xinyu in Linjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 父仲華，侍祖鬱官鄂州。

translations.literal: His father Zhonghua attended upon his grandfather Yu, who served as an official in Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhonghua served his grandfather Yu while Yu held office in Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 會。

translations.literal: At that time.
translations.idiomatic: Just then.

sentences.zh: 江水暴至，徙家黃鶴樓，漢陽人望見樓上若有光景，是夕，欽若生。

translations.literal: The Yangzi surged suddenly; the family moved to the Yellow Crane Tower. People of Hanyang saw on the tower what seemed to be a luminous glow. That night, Qinruo was born.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yangzi flooded without warning, the family relocated to the Yellow Crane Tower. From across the river in Hanyang, people saw what looked like a glow on the tower. That very night, Qinruo was born.

sentences.zh: 欽若早孤，鬱愛之。

translations.literal: Qinruo lost his father early; Yu cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo lost his father while still young, and Yu doted on him.

sentences.zh: 太宗伐太原時，欽若才十八，作《平晉賦論》獻行在。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong attacked Taiyuan, Qinruo was only eighteen. He composed "An Essay on the Pacification of Jin" and presented it at the imperial headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizong's campaign against Taiyuan, the eighteen-year-old Qinruo wrote "An Essay on the Pacification of Jin" and presented it to the emperor's field camp.

sentences.zh: 鬱為濠州判官，將死，告家人曰：「吾曆官逾五十年，慎於用刑，活人多矣，後必有興者，其在吾孫乎！」

translations.literal: Yu served as judge in Haozhou. On the verge of death, he told his family: "I have held office for more than fifty years and have been cautious in applying punishment, sparing many lives. Surely someone among our descendants will rise to prominence — might it be my grandson?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yu, serving as judge in Haozhou, was near death, he told his family: "In more than fifty years of office I have been sparing with punishments and saved many lives. Our house will surely produce someone of distinction someday — perhaps it will be my grandson!"

sentences.zh: 欽若擢進士甲科，為亳州防禦推官，遷秘書省秘書郎，監廬州稅。

translations.literal: Qinruo passed the jinshi examination in the first rank, was appointed Deputy Magistrate for Defense in Bozhou, was transferred to Secretary in the Secretariat, and supervised taxation in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo earned first place on the jinshi examination, served as deputy magistrate for defense in Bozhou, was promoted to secretary in the Secretariat, and supervised tax collection in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 改太常丞、判三司理欠憑由司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently directed the Three Departments Office for Recovery of Arrears and Verification of Vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently oversaw the Three Departments office that recovered back taxes and verified fiscal records.

sentences.zh: 時毋賓古為度支判官，嘗言曰：「天下逋負，自五代迄今，理督未已，民病幾不能勝矣。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Binggu served as judge of the Revenue Office. He once said: "Arrears owed throughout the realm, from the Five Dynasties to the present, have been pursued without cease. The people's suffering has nearly become unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Binggu, then judge of the Revenue Office, had once remarked: "From the Five Dynasties down to today the state has never stopped pursuing unpaid debts nationwide, and the people can scarcely endure the burden anymore.

sentences.zh: 仆將啟蠲之。」

translations.literal: I intend to propose their remission."
translations.idiomatic: I mean to ask that they be waived."

sentences.zh: 欽若一夕命吏勾校成數，翌日上之。

translations.literal: In a single night Qinruo ordered clerks to tally the full amount, and the next day submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo had clerks calculate the total in one night and presented the figures the following morning.

sentences.zh: 真宗大驚曰：「先帝顧不知邪？」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong was greatly shocked and said: "Could the late emperor truly have been unaware of this?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong was astonished. "Could my predecessor really not have known?" he said."

sentences.zh: 欽若徐曰：「先帝固知之，殆留與陛下收人心爾。」

translations.literal: Qinruo replied calmly: "The late emperor surely did know; he likely reserved this for Your Majesty to win the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo answered evenly: "He certainly knew — he probably left this for Your Majesty as a means to win the people's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 即日放逋負一千餘萬，釋係囚三千餘人。

translations.literal: That same day more than ten million in arrears were remitted and more than three thousand prisoners in custody were released.
translations.idiomatic: On the spot he forgave more than ten million in unpaid debts and released over three thousand detainees.

sentences.zh: 帝益器重欽若，召試學士院，拜右正言、知制誥，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: The emperor valued Qinruo all the more, summoned him for examination at the Hanlin Academy, appointed him Right Remonstrator and Drafting Secretary for Imperial Edicts, and summoned him as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to rely on Qinruo even more heavily, had him examined at the Hanlin Academy, appointed him right remonstrator and drafter of edicts, and then inducted him as a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 蜀寇王均始平，為西川安撫使。

translations.literal: When the Shu bandit Wang Jun had just been pacified, he was made Pacification Commissioner of Western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion of Wang Jun in Shu was finally suppressed, Qinruo was appointed pacification commissioner for western Shu.

sentences.zh: 所至問繫囚，自死罪以下第降之，凡列便宜，多所施行。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he inquired after prisoners in custody and reduced sentences step by step from capital crimes downward; of every proposal for expedient measures he put many into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he went he reviewed detained prisoners and reduced penalties below the death sentence, implementing many of the practical reforms he proposed along the way.

sentences.zh: 還，授左諫議大夫、參知政事，以郊祀恩，加給事中。

translations.literal: Upon returning he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief and Participant in State Affairs; by grace of the suburban sacrifice he was further made Supervisory Censor.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made left censor-in-chief and vice grand councilor, and received the additional title of supervisory censor in recognition of the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 河陰民常德方訟臨津縣尉任懿賂欽若得中第，事下御史臺劾治。

translations.literal: Chang Defang, a commoner of Heyin, sued Linjin County Magistrate Ren Yi for bribing Qinruo to obtain a passing rank. The case was referred to the Censorate for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Heyin named Chang Defang accused the Linjin county magistrate Ren Yi of bribing Qinruo to pass the examinations, and the case was sent to the Censorate for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 初，欽若咸平中嘗知貢舉，懿舉諸科，寓僧仁雅舍。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Xianping era Qinruo had served as chief examiner. Yi was taking the special examinations and lodged at the residence of the monk Ren Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, during the Xianping period Qinruo had overseen the metropolitan examinations. Ren Yi was sitting for the special examinations and was staying at the home of the monk Ren Ya.

sentences.zh: 仁雅識僧惠秦者與欽若厚，懿與惠秦約，以銀三百五十兩賂欽若，書其數於紙，令惠秦持去。

translations.literal: Ren Ya knew a monk named Hui Qin who was on close terms with Qinruo. Yi made an arrangement with Hui Qin to bribe Qinruo with three hundred and fifty taels of silver, wrote the amount on paper, and had Hui Qin take it away.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Ya knew a monk named Hui Qin who was close to Qinruo. Ren Yi arranged with Hui Qin to bribe Qinruo with three hundred and fifty taels of silver, wrote down the sum on a slip of paper, and had Hui Qin carry it off.

sentences.zh: 會欽若已入院，屬欽若客納所書於欽若妻李氏，惠秦減所書銀百兩，欲自取之。

translations.literal: It happened that Qinruo had already entered the examination hall. A client of Qinruo's accepted the written note and handed it to Qinruo's wife, Lady Li. Hui Qin reduced the written amount by one hundred taels of silver, intending to keep it for himself.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qinruo had already entered the examination hall. One of his clients took the note and passed it to Qinruo's wife, Lady Li, while Hui Qin shaved one hundred taels off the amount written on the slip, planning to pocket the difference.

sentences.zh: 李氏令奴祁睿書懿名於臂，並以所約銀告欽若。

translations.literal: Lady Li had the servant Qi Rui write Yi's name on his arm and also informed Qinruo of the agreed amount of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li had her servant Qi Rui write Ren Yi's name on his arm and reported the agreed bribe to Qinruo.

sentences.zh: 懿再入試第五場，睿復持湯飲至貢院，欽若密令奴索取銀，懿未即與而登科去。

translations.literal: When Yi entered the fifth examination session, Qi Rui again brought soup and drink to the examination compound. Qinruo secretly ordered the servant to demand the silver. Yi did not immediately pay but passed the examination and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Yi entered the fifth round of examinations, Qi Rui once again brought refreshments to the examination grounds. Qinruo secretly instructed the servant to collect the silver, but Ren Yi had not yet paid when he passed the exams and left.

sentences.zh: 仁雅馳書河陰，始歸之。

translations.literal: Ren Ya sent a letter in haste to Heyin, and only then was it returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Ya hurried a letter to Heyin, and only then was the silver returned.

sentences.zh: 德方得其書，以告御史中丞趙昌言，昌言以聞。

translations.literal: Defang obtained the letter and reported it to Censor-in-Chief Zhao Changyan, who reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Defang obtained the letter and informed Censor-in-Chief Zhao Changyan, who reported the matter to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 既捕祁睿等，亦請逮欽若屬吏。

translations.literal: Once Qi Rui and the others were arrested, they also requested that Qinruo be taken into custody as a subject of the case.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi Rui and the others were arrested, they also asked that Qinruo be detained and handed over to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 祁睿本亳小吏，雖從欽若久，而名猶隸亳州。

translations.literal: Qi Rui was originally a minor clerk of Bozhou. Although he had long followed Qinruo, his name was still registered in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Rui had originally been a minor clerk in Bozhou. Though he had served Qinruo for years, his registration still belonged to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 欽若乃言：「向未有祁睿，惠秦亦不及門。」

translations.literal: Qinruo then said: "If Qi Rui had not existed in the past, Hui Qin would never have reached my door either."
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo then claimed: "If Qi Rui had never existed, Hui Qin would never have come to my door in the first place."

sentences.zh: 帝方顧欽若厚，命邢昺、閻承翰等於太常寺別鞫之。

translations.literal: The emperor was at that time favorably disposed toward Qinruo and ordered Xing Bing, Yan Chenghan, and others to conduct a separate inquiry at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then strongly inclined toward Qinruo and ordered Xing Bing, Yan Chenghan, and others to hold a separate hearing at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 懿更雲妻兄張駕識知舉官洪湛，嘗俱造湛門。

translations.literal: Yi further claimed that his wife's elder brother Zhang Jia knew the chief examiner Hong Zhan and that they had once visited Hong's residence together.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yi further stated that his wife's elder brother Zhang Jia knew chief examiner Hong Zhan and that the two of them had once called together at Hong's gate.

sentences.zh: 始但以銀屬二僧，不知達主司為誰。

translations.literal: At first they had only entrusted the silver to the two monks, not knowing which chief examiner it would reach.
translations.idiomatic: At first they had merely entrusted the silver to the two monks, without knowing which examiner it would ultimately reach.

sentences.zh: 昺等遂誣湛受懿銀，湛適使陝西還，而獄已具。

translations.literal: Xing and the others then falsely accused Hong of accepting silver from Yi. Hong happened to be returning from a mission to Shaanxi, but the case was already complete.
translations.idiomatic: Xing and his colleagues then falsely charged Hong with accepting Ren Yi's bribe. Hong happened to be returning from a mission to Shaanxi, but the case had already been finalized.

sentences.zh: 時駕且死，睿又悉遁去，欽若因得固執祁睿休役後始傭於家，它奴使多新募，不識惠秦，故皆無證驗。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Jia was near death, and Qi Rui had also fled entirely. Qinruo was thus able to insist that Qi Rui had only been hired in his household after completing his labor service, that most of the other servants were newly recruited and did not know Hui Qin, and so there was no corroborating evidence in any case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jia was by then near death, and Qi Rui had fled altogether. Qinruo was therefore able to maintain that Qi Rui had been hired only after completing his corvée service, that most of the other servants were newly recruited and did not know Hui Qin, and that there was no corroborating evidence at all.

sentences.zh: 湛坐削藉、流儋州，而欽若遂免。

translations.literal: Hong was punished by stripping of his credentials and exile to Danzhou, while Qinruo was thus spared.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was stripped of his credentials and exiled to Danzhou, while Qinruo escaped punishment entirely.

sentences.zh: 方湛代王旦入知貢舉，懿已試第三場，及官收湛贓，家無有也，乃以湛假梁顥白金器輸官，湛遂死貶所。

translations.literal: When Hong replaced Wang Dan as chief examiner, Yi had already completed the third examination session. When officials searched Hong's home for the bribe, there was nothing to be found. Hong therefore surrendered to the authorities white-gold vessels he had borrowed from Liang Hao, and Hong died in his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong replaced Wang Dan as chief examiner, Ren Yi had already completed the third round of tests. When officials searched Hong's home for the bribe, they found nothing, so Hong turned over to the authorities white-gold vessels he had borrowed from Liang Hao. He died in exile.

sentences.zh: 人知其冤，而欽若恃勢，人莫敢言者。

translations.literal: People knew he had been wronged, but Qinruo relied on his power, and no one dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew Hong had been wronged, but Qinruo wielded such power that no one dared say so openly.

sentences.zh: 景德初，契丹入寇，帝將幸澶淵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era the Khitan invaded, and the emperor was about to visit Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era, when the Khitan invaded, the emperor prepared to go in person to Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 欽若自請北行，以工部侍郎、參知政事判天雄軍、提舉河北轉運司，真宗親宴以遣之。

translations.literal: Qinruo volunteered to go north. As Vice Minister of Works and Participant in State Affairs he was assigned to oversee the Tianxiong Army and to direct the Hebei transport commission. Emperor Zhenzong personally hosted a banquet to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo volunteered to go north and was appointed vice minister of works and vice grand councilor with authority over the Tianxiong Army and the Hebei transport commission. Emperor Zhenzong personally held a farewell banquet for him.

sentences.zh: 素與寇準不協，及還，累表願解政事，罷為刑部侍郎、資政殿學士。

translations.literal: He had long been at odds with Kou Zhun. Upon returning he repeatedly submitted memorials asking to be relieved of state affairs and was removed to Vice Minister of Justice and Academician of the Hall of Esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been at odds with Kou Zhun. After returning he repeatedly asked to leave the grand council, and was relieved to vice minister of justice and academician of the Hall of Esteem.

sentences.zh: 尋判尚書都省，修《冊府元龜》，或褒讚所及，欽若自名表首以謝，即繆誤有所譴問，戒書吏但云楊億以下，其所為多此類也。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was assigned to oversee the Ministry of Personnel and compiled the Prime Repository of Literary Treasures. When praise was involved, Qinruo would sign his own name at the head of the memorial of thanks; if there were errors for which blame was assigned, he instructed the clerks to say only "below Yang Yi." Much of what he did was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and helped compile the Prime Repository of Literary Treasures. When praise was due, Qinruo put his own name at the top of the thank-you memorial; when mistakes brought reprimands, he told the clerks to say only "from Yang Yi downward." He behaved this way in many matters.

sentences.zh: 歲中，改兵部，升大學士、知通進銀台司兼門下封駁事。

translations.literal: Within the year he was transferred to the Ministry of War, promoted to Senior Academician, and made Director of the Gateway for Memorials and Silver Terrace Office with concurrent responsibility for censorial review under the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was moved to the Ministry of War, elevated to senior academician, and made director of the Gateway for Memorials and Silver Terrace Office with concurrent censorial review duties under the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，欽若罷，為置資政殿學士以寵之，準定其班在翰林學士下。

translations.literal: When Qinruo had first been removed from office, the post of Academician of the Hall of Esteem was created to honor him. Kou Zhun fixed its rank below that of Hanlin Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinruo was first removed from the grand council, the post of academician of the Hall of Esteem was created to honor him, and Kou Zhun set its rank below that of Hanlin academicians.

sentences.zh: 欽若訴於帝，復加「大」字，班承旨上。

translations.literal: Qinruo appealed to the emperor, the prefix "Senior" was restored to the title, and its rank was placed above that of the Chief Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo appealed to the emperor, who restored the prefix "Senior" to the title and placed its rank above that of the chief academician.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左丞知樞密院事，修國史。

translations.literal: As Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel he directed the Bureau of Military Affairs and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: As left vice director of the Ministry of Personnel he directed the Bureau of Military Affairs and oversaw compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，為封禪經度制置使兼判兗州，為天書儀衛副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong xiangfu era he was made Commissioner for the Preparatory Arrangements of the Fengshan Sacrifice with concurrent jurisdiction over Yanzhou, and served as Deputy Director of Rites for the Heavenly Writ.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong xiangfu era he became commissioner for the preparatory arrangements of the Fengshan sacrifice with concurrent jurisdiction over Yanzhou, and served as deputy director of rites for the Heavenly Writ.

sentences.zh: 先是，真宗嘗夢神人言「賜天書於泰山」，即密諭欽若。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Zhenzong had dreamed that a divine being said, "A Heavenly Writ is bestowed upon Mount Tai," and he secretly informed Qinruo of this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Zhenzong had dreamed that a divine being said, "A Heavenly Writ is bestowed upon Mount Tai," and he secretly told Qinruo of the dream.

sentences.zh: 欽若因言，六月甲午，木工董祚於醴泉亭北見黃素曳草上，有字不能識，皇城吏王居正見其上有御名，以告。

translations.literal: Qinruo then reported that on the jiawu day of the sixth month the carpenter Dong Zuo, north of the Liquan Pavilion, saw yellow silk dragging along the grass with writing he could not read. The palace official Wang Juzheng saw the emperor's name inscribed upon it and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo then reported that on the jiawu day of the sixth month, north of the Liquan Pavilion, the carpenter Dong Zuo saw yellow silk trailing through the grass with writing he could not decipher. The palace official Wang Juzheng noticed the emperor's name on it and reported the discovery.

sentences.zh: 欽若既得之，具威儀奉導至社首，跪授中使，馳奉以進。

translations.literal: Once Qinruo obtained it, he assembled full ceremonial guard to conduct it to Sheshou, knelt to hand it to the palace envoy, who rushed it forward as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qinruo had obtained it, he assembled full ceremonial escort to conduct it to Sheshou, knelt to hand it to a palace envoy, who rushed it to the capital as tribute.

sentences.zh: 真宗至含芳園奉迎，出所上《天書再降祥瑞圖》示百僚。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong went to Hanfang Garden to receive it in ceremony and showed the ministers the "Chart of the Second Descent of the Heavenly Writ and Auspicious Signs" that had been submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong went to Hanfang Garden to receive it in ceremony and showed his ministers the "Chart of the Second Descent of the Heavenly Writ and Auspicious Signs" that had been submitted.

sentences.zh: 欽若又言至嶽下兩夢神人，願增建廟庭。

translations.literal: Qinruo also said that upon reaching the foot of the mountain he twice dreamed of a divine being who wished to expand the temple precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo also reported that after reaching the foot of the mountain he twice dreamed of a divine being who wished to enlarge the temple precincts.

sentences.zh: 及至威雄將軍廟，其神像如夢中所見，因請構亭廟中。

translations.literal: When they arrived at the Weixiong General's Shrine, the image of the deity matched what he had seen in his dreams, and he therefore requested that a pavilion be built within the temple.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Shrine of the Weixiong General, the deity's image matched what he had seen in his dreams, and he requested that a pavilion be built within the temple.

sentences.zh: 封禪禮成，遷禮部尚書，命作《社首頌》，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Fengshan rites were completed, he was promoted to Minister of Rites and ordered to compose "An Ode to Sheshou," then transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After the Fengshan rites were completed, he was promoted to minister of rites and ordered to compose "An Ode to Sheshou," then transferred to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 從祀汾陰，復為天書儀衛副使，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Following the sacrifice at Fenyin, he again served as Deputy Director of Rites for the Heavenly Writ and was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After accompanying the sacrifice at Fenyin, he again served as deputy director of rites for the Heavenly Writ and was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 明年，為樞密使、檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The following year he became Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Honorary Grand Preceptor, and Grand Councilor with equal standing at the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, honorary grand preceptor, and grand councilor with equal standing at the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 初，學士晁迥草制，誤削去官，有詔仍帶吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At first the academician Chao Yuan drafted the appointment edict but mistakenly omitted his official titles. An edict was issued that he should still retain the title of Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When academician Chao Yuan first drafted the appointment edict, he mistakenly omitted Qinruo's official titles, so an edict was issued directing that he retain the title of minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 聖祖降，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When the Sage Ancestor descended, he was given the additional honorary title of Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sage Ancestor descended, he received the additional honorary title of grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 欽若居第在太廟後壖，自言出入訶導不自安，因易賜官第於安定坊。

translations.literal: Qinruo's residence stood behind the wall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple. He said that entering and leaving under shouted escort made him uneasy, and so an official residence in Anding Ward was exchanged for his own.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo's residence stood just behind the wall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple. He said he felt uneasy going in and out under shouted escort, so an official residence in Anding Ward was exchanged for his own.

sentences.zh: 七年，為同天書刻玉使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he served as Commissioner for Carving the Heavenly Writ on Jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he served as commissioner for carving the Heavenly Writ on jade.

sentences.zh: 馬知節同在樞密，素惡欽若，議論不相下。

translations.literal: Ma Zhijie served together with him in the Bureau of Military Affairs, had long disliked Qinruo, and their views clashed without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhijie served with him in the Bureau of Military Affairs, had long disliked Qinruo, and their opinions clashed without either yielding.

sentences.zh: 會瀘州都巡檢王懷信等上平蠻功，欽若久不決，知節因面詆其短，爭於帝前。

translations.literal: When the patrol inspectors of Luzhou, including Wang Huaixin, submitted merit reports for suppressing barbarian tribes, Qinruo delayed a decision for a long time. Zhijie took the opportunity to openly denounce his shortcomings, and they argued before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Luzhou patrol inspectors including Wang Huaixin submitted reports of merit for pacifying tribal forces, Qinruo delayed a decision for a long time. Zhijie seized the occasion to denounce his failings to his face, and the two quarreled before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及趣論賞，欽若遂擅除懷信等官，坐是，罷樞密使，奉朝請。

translations.literal: When the emperor pressed for a decision on rewards, Qinruo arbitrarily promoted Huaixin and the others to office. For this he was removed as Director of Military Affairs and remained only as court attendee.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor pressed for a decision on rewards, Qinruo arbitrarily promoted Huaixin and the others. For this he was removed as director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and reduced to court attendee.

sentences.zh: 改刻玉副使、知通進銀台司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Deputy Commissioner for Jade Carving and Director of the Gateway for Memorials and Silver Terrace Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as deputy commissioner for jade carving and director of the Gateway for Memorials and Silver Terrace Office.

sentences.zh: 復拜樞密使、同平章事。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Director of Military Affairs and Grand Councilor with equal standing.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and grand councilor with equal standing.

sentences.zh: 上玉皇尊號，遷尚書右僕射、判禮儀院，為會靈觀使。

translations.literal: When the honorific title was conferred upon the Jade Emperor, he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, assigned to the Court of Ceremonial, and made Commissioner of the Huiling Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jade Emperor received his honorific title, Qinruo was promoted to right vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, placed in charge of the Court of Ceremonial, and made commissioner of the Huiling Temple.

sentences.zh: 有龜蛇見拱聖營，因其地建詳源觀，命欽若總領之。

translations.literal: When a tortoise and serpent appeared at Gong Sheng Camp, the Xiangyuan Temple was built on that spot, and Qinruo was placed in overall charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: When a tortoise and serpent were sighted at Gong Sheng Camp, the Xiangyuan Temple was built on the spot, and Qinruo was placed in overall charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 尋拜左僕射兼中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Left Vice Director and Vice Minister of the Secretariat as Grand Councilor with equal standing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed left vice director and vice minister of the Secretariat as grand councilor with equal standing.

sentences.zh: 明年，為景靈使，閱《道藏》，得趙氏神仙事跡四十人，繪於廊廡。

translations.literal: The next year he became Commissioner of the Jingling Temple, reviewed the Daoist Canon, found records of forty figures from the Zhao clan who achieved immortality, and had them painted in the cloister galleries.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became commissioner of the Jingling Temple, reviewed the Daoist Canon, found accounts of forty Zhao clansmen who had attained immortality, and had them painted in the cloister galleries.

sentences.zh: 又明年，商州捕得道士譙文易，畜禁書，能以術使六丁六甲神，自言嘗出入欽若家，得欽若所遺詩。

translations.literal: The year after that, a Daoist named Qiao Wenyi was captured in Shangzhou. He possessed forbidden texts and claimed that by arts he could command the Six Jia spirits. He said he had once come and gone from Qinruo's household and possessed poetry Qinruo had given him.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, a Daoist named Qiao Wenyi was arrested in Shangzhou. He kept forbidden texts and claimed he could summon the Six Jia spirits by occult arts. He said he had frequented Qinruo's residence and possessed poems Qinruo had given him.

sentences.zh: 帝以問欽若，謝不省，遂以太子太保出判杭州。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Qinruo about this. He pleaded ignorance and was sent out as Honorary Grand Tutor to govern Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Qinruo about the matter. He pleaded ignorance and was sent out as honorary grand tutor to govern Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇太子，自以東宮師保請歸朝，復為資政大學士。

translations.literal: When Renzong was crown prince, Qinruo requested to return to court as tutor to the Eastern Palace and was reappointed Senior Academician of the Hall of Esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, Qinruo asked to return to court as tutor to the Eastern Palace and was reappointed senior academician of the Hall of Esteem.

sentences.zh: 詔日赴資善堂侍講皇太子。

translations.literal: An edict directed him to attend the Hall of Excellent Virtue daily to lecture the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed him to go daily to the Hall of Excellent Virtue to lecture the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 會輔臣兼領三少，欽若以品高求換秩，拜司空，尋除山南道節度使、同平章事、判河南府。

translations.literal: When senior ministers concurrently held the three junior tutorships, Qinruo, considering his rank too high for such a role, sought an exchange of rank and was appointed Minister of Works. Soon afterward he was made Military Commissioner of the Southern Shan Circuit as Grand Councilor and governor of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When senior ministers were concurrently holding the three junior tutorships, Qinruo, considering his rank too high for such a post, sought a change of rank and was appointed minister of works. He was soon made military commissioner of the Southern Shan Circuit as grand councilor and governor of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 與宰相丁謂不相悅，以疾請就醫京師，不報。

translations.literal: He was on bad terms with Grand Councilor Ding Wei and, pleading illness, requested medical treatment in the capital but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He was on bad terms with Grand Councilor Ding Wei and, pleading illness, asked to receive medical treatment in the capital, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 令其子從益移文河南府，輿疾而歸。

translations.literal: He had his son Congyi send a petition to Henan Prefecture, and Qinruo returned home carried in a litter despite his illness.
translations.idiomatic: He had his son Congyi send a formal notice to Henan Prefecture, and Qinruo returned home carried in a litter despite his illness.

sentences.zh: 謂言欽若擅去官守，命御史中丞薛映就第按問。

translations.literal: Ding Wei said that Qinruo had left his post without authorization and ordered Censor-in-Chief Xue Ying to go to his residence to investigate and question him.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei charged that Qinruo had abandoned his post without authorization and ordered Censor-in-Chief Xue Ying to go to his residence to investigate.

sentences.zh: 欽若惶恐伏罪，降司農卿、分司南京，奪從益一官。

translations.literal: Qinruo, terrified, confessed his guilt. He was demoted to Director of the Directorate of Agriculture with duties at the Southern Capital, and Congyi was stripped of one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo, terrified, confessed his guilt. He was demoted to director of the Directorate of Agriculture with duties at the Southern Capital, and Congyi was stripped of one rank.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，改秘書監，起為太常卿、知濠州，以刑部尚書知江寧府。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, Qinruo was transferred to Director of the Imperial Library, recalled as Director of Imperial Sacrifices governing Haozhou, then made Minister of Justice governing Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne, Qinruo was transferred to director of the Imperial Library, recalled as director of imperial sacrifices to govern Haozhou, and then made minister of justice to govern Jiangning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗為飛白書，適欽若有奏至，因大書「王欽若」字。

translations.literal: Renzong once wrote in flying-white script. Just as a memorial from Qinruo arrived, he boldly wrote the characters "Wang Qinruo."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong once practiced flying-white calligraphy. Just as a memorial from Qinruo arrived, he boldly wrote the characters "Wang Qinruo."

sentences.zh: 是時，馮拯病，太后有再相欽若意，即取字緘置湯藥合，遣中人齎以賜，且口宣召之。

translations.literal: At that time Feng Zheng was ill, and the empress dowager intended to appoint Qinruo grand councilor again. She sealed the characters in a medicine box, sent a palace envoy with gifts, and orally summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Feng Zheng was ill, and the empress dowager intended to appoint Qinruo grand councilor again. She sealed the characters in a medicine box, sent a palace envoy with gifts, and orally summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 至國門而人未有知者。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital gates, no one yet knew of this.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the capital gates, no one yet knew of the summons.

sentences.zh: 既朝，復拜司空、門下侍郎、同平章事、玉清昭應宮使、昭文館大學士，監修國史。

translations.literal: After attending court he was again appointed Minister of Works, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, Commissioner of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace, Senior Academician of the Academy of Literary Glory, and overseer of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: After attending court he was again appointed minister of works, vice minister of the Secretariat, grand councilor, commissioner of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace, senior academician of the Academy of Literary Glory, and overseer of the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 帝初臨政，欽若謂平時百官敘進，皆有常法，為《遷敘圖》以獻。

translations.literal: When the emperor was first administering affairs directly, Qinruo observed that the usual promotions for all officials followed fixed rules and presented a "Chart of Advancement by Seniority" to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first began to administer affairs directly, Qinruo observed that the usual promotions for all officials followed fixed rules and presented a "Chart of Advancement by Seniority" to the throne.

sentences.zh: 《真宗實錄》成，進司徒，以郊祀恩，封冀國公。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Zhenzong was completed, he was promoted to Minister of Education and, by grace of the suburban sacrifice, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Zhenzong was completed, he was promoted to minister of education and, by grace of the suburban sacrifice, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 知邵武軍吳植病，求外徙，因殿中丞餘諤以黃金遺欽若，未至，而植復遣牙吏至欽若第問之。

translations.literal: Wu Zhi, prefect of Shaowu Circuit, fell ill and requested transfer elsewhere. Through Palace Censor Yu'e he sent gold as a gift to Qinruo. Before it arrived, Wu again sent his clerk to Qinruo's residence to inquire about it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhi, prefect of Shaowu Circuit, fell ill and asked to be transferred elsewhere. Through palace censor Yu'e he sent gold as a gift to Qinruo. Before it arrived, Wu sent his clerk again to Qinruo's residence to inquire about it.

sentences.zh: 欽若執以送官，植、諤皆坐貶。

translations.literal: Qinruo detained the messenger and turned him over to the authorities. Both Wu and Yu'e were punished with demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo detained the messenger and turned him over to the authorities. Both Wu and Yu'e were demoted.

sentences.zh: 初，欽若安撫西川，植為新繁縣尉，嘗嘗薦舉之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qinruo pacified western Sichuan, Wu had been magistrate of Xinfan County and Qinruo had once recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qinruo pacified western Sichuan, Wu had been magistrate of Xinfan County and Qinruo had once recommended him.

sentences.zh: 至是，亦當以失舉坐罪，詔勿問。

translations.literal: At this point he should also have been punished for failed recommendation, but an edict directed that this not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: By rights he should also have been punished for a failed recommendation, but an edict directed that the matter not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 兼譯經使，始赴傳法院，感疾亟歸。

translations.literal: As Commissioner for Translation of Scriptures, he first went to the Sutra Translation Court but fell seriously ill and returned quickly.
translations.idiomatic: As commissioner for translation of scriptures, he first went to the Sutra Translation Court but fell seriously ill and hurried home.

sentences.zh: 帝臨問，賜白金五千兩。

translations.literal: The emperor visited him in inquiry and bestowed five thousand taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited him in person and bestowed five thousand taels of white silver.

sentences.zh: 既卒，贈太師、中書令，諡文穆，錄親屬及所親信二十餘人。

translations.literal: After his death he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, given the posthumous name Wenmu, and more than twenty relatives and close associates were given official appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored as grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat, given the posthumous name Wenmu, and more than twenty relatives and close associates were granted official appointments.

sentences.zh: 國朝以來宰相恤恩，未有欽若比者。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the dynasty, no grand councilor's posthumous generosity has matched Qinruo's.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, no grand councilor had received posthumous favors comparable to Qinruo's.

sentences.zh: 欽若嘗言：「少時過圃田，夜起視天中，赤文成『紫微』字。

translations.literal: Qinruo once said: "When I was young I passed through Putian. I rose at night and looked up at the sky, where red writing formed the characters 'Ziwei.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo once said: "When I was young I passed through Putian. I rose at night and looked up at the sky, where red writing formed the characters 'Ziwei.

sentences.zh: 後使蜀，至褒城道中，遇異人，告以他日位至宰相。

translations.literal: Later, while serving in Shu, on the road to Baocheng I met a strange man who told me that one day I would reach the rank of grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while serving in Shu, on the road to Baocheng I met a strange man who told me that one day I would reach the rank of grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 既去，視其刺字，則唐相裴度也。」

translations.literal: After he left, I looked at his name card, and it was the Tang grand councilor Pei Du."
translations.idiomatic: After he left, I looked at his name card, and it was the Tang grand councilor Pei Du."

sentences.zh: 及貴，遂好神仙之事，常用道家科儀建壇場以禮神，朱書「紫微」二字陳於壇上。

translations.literal: Once he had risen to high position, he devoted himself to matters of immortals, regularly using Daoist ritual to establish altars for worship, and placed the two characters "Ziwei" written in cinnabar upon the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had risen to high position, he devoted himself to matters of immortals, regularly using Daoist ritual to establish altars for worship, and placed the two characters "Ziwei" written in cinnabar upon the altar.

sentences.zh: 表修裴度祠於圃田，官其裔孫，自撰文以紀其事。

translations.literal: He memorialized to repair the shrine of Pei Du at Putian, had Pei's descendants given official rank, and himself composed a text to commemorate the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to repair the shrine of Pei Du at Putian, had Pei's descendants given official rank, and himself composed a text to commemorate the affair.

sentences.zh: 真宗封泰山、祀汾陰，而天下爭言符瑞，皆欽若與丁謂倡之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong performed the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai and sacrificed at Fenyin, and throughout the realm people competed to report omens and auspicious signs — all of this Qinruo and Ding Wei pioneered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong performed the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai and sacrificed at Fenyin, and throughout the realm people competed to report omens and auspicious signs — all of this Qinruo and Ding Wei had pioneered.

sentences.zh: 嘗建議躬謁元德皇太后別廟，為莊穆皇后行期服。

translations.literal: He once proposed that the emperor personally visit the separate temple of Empress Dowager Yuande and observe the full mourning period for Empress Zhuangmu.
translations.idiomatic: He once proposed that the emperor personally visit the separate temple of Empress Dowager Yuande and observe full mourning for Empress Zhuangmu.

sentences.zh: 議者以謂天子當絕傍期，欽若所言不合禮。

translations.literal: Critics held that the Son of Heaven should terminate collateral mourning at the proper point, and that what Qinruo said did not accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that the emperor should terminate collateral mourning at the proper point, and that Qinruo's proposal did not accord with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 又請置先蠶並壽星祠，升天皇北極帝坐於郊壇第一龕，增執法、孫星位，別製王公以下車輅、鼓吹，以備拜官、婚葬。

translations.literal: He also requested the establishment of shrines to the First Silkworm and the Longevity Star, the elevation of the seats of the Celestial Emperor and the Northern Pole Emperor to the first niches of the suburban altar, the addition of positions for the Law-Enforcing and Grandson Stars, and the separate manufacture of carriages, canopies, and musical escort for princes and officials downward, to be used for investiture, weddings, and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested shrines to the First Silkworm and the Longevity Star, elevation of the Celestial Emperor and Northern Pole Emperor to the first niches of the suburban altar, addition of positions for the Law-Enforcing and Grandson Stars, and separate carriages, canopies, and musical escort for princes and officials downward for use at investitures, weddings, and funerals.

sentences.zh: 所著書有《鹵簿記》、《彤管懿範》、《天書儀製》、《聖祖事跡》、《翊聖真君傳》、《五嶽廣聞記》、《列宿萬靈朝真圖》、《羅天大醮儀》。

translations.literal: Among the books he authored were Records of Imperial Escort, Exemplary Models of the Red Tube, Rites for the Heavenly Writ, Deeds of the Sage Ancestor, Biography of the True Lord Who Assists the Sage, Broad Records Heard from the Five Sacred Peaks, Chart of the Ten Thousand Spirits of the Constellations Paying Homage to the True, and Rites of the Grand Altar of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Among the books he authored were Records of Imperial Escort, Exemplary Models of the Red Tube, Rites for the Heavenly Writ, Deeds of the Sage Ancestor, Biography of the True Lord Who Assists the Sage, Broad Records Heard from the Five Sacred Peaks, Chart of the Ten Thousand Spirits of the Constellations Paying Homage to the True, and Rites of the Grand Altar of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 欽若自以深達道教，多所建明，領校道書，凡增六百餘卷。

translations.literal: Qinruo considered himself deeply versed in the Daoist teaching, made many proposals and clarifications, and supervised collation of Daoist texts, adding more than six hundred volumes in all.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo considered himself deeply versed in Daoist teaching, made many proposals and clarifications, and supervised collation of Daoist texts, adding more than six hundred volumes in all.

sentences.zh: 欽若狀貌短小，項有附疣，時人目為「癭相」。

translations.literal: Qinruo was short in stature and had a wen on his neck; people of the time called him "the goitered grand councilor."
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo was short in stature and had a wen on his neck; people of the time called him "the goitered grand councilor."

sentences.zh: 然智數過人，每朝廷有所興造，委曲遷就，以中帝意。

translations.literal: Yet his cunning surpassed that of others. Whenever the court undertook some new project, he would tactfully adapt himself to hit the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his cunning surpassed that of others. Whenever the court undertook some new project, he would tactfully adapt himself to satisfy the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 又性傾巧，敢為矯誕。

translations.literal: Moreover, by nature he was inclined to artifice and dared to engage in pretense and fabrication.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, by nature he was inclined to artifice and dared to engage in pretense and fabrication.

sentences.zh: 馬知節嘗斥其奸狀，帝亦不之罪。

translations.literal: Ma Zhijie once denounced his treacherous conduct, but the emperor did not punish him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhijie once denounced his treacherous conduct, but the emperor did not punish him for it.

sentences.zh: 其後仁宗嘗謂輔臣曰：「欽若久在政府，觀其所為，真奸邪也。」

translations.literal: Later Renzong once said to his senior ministers: "Qinruo has long been in the government. Judging from his conduct, he is truly treacherous and corrupt."
translations.idiomatic: Later Renzong once said to his senior ministers: "Qinruo has long been in the government. Judging from his conduct, he is truly treacherous and corrupt."

sentences.zh: 王曾對曰：「欽若與丁謂、林特、陳彭年、劉承珪，時謂之『五鬼』。

translations.literal: Wang Zeng replied: "Qinruo, together with Ding Wei, Lin Te, Chen Pengnian, and Liu Chenggui, were at the time called the 'Five Demons.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng replied: "Qinruo, together with Ding Wei, Lin Te, Chen Pengnian, and Liu Chenggui, were at the time called the 'Five Demons.

sentences.zh: 奸邪險偽，誠如聖諭。」

translations.literal: Treacherous, corrupt, dangerous, and false — it is truly as Your Majesty has said."
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous, corrupt, dangerous, and false — it is truly as Your Majesty has said."

sentences.zh: 欽若子從益，終讚善大夫，追賜進士及第。

translations.literal: Qinruo's son Congyi ended as Master of Excellent Goodness and was posthumously granted the status of having passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo's son Congyi ended as master of excellent goodness and was posthumously granted the status of having passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 後無子，以叔之子為後。

translations.literal: Later he had no son and took his uncle's son as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Later he had no son and took his uncle's son as heir.

translations.literal: [Supplement]
translations.idiomatic: [Supplement]

sentences.zh: 林特

translations.literal: Lin Te
translations.idiomatic: Lin Te

sentences.zh: 林特字士奇。

translations.literal: Lin Te, styled Shiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Te, courtesy name Shiqing.

sentences.zh: 祖揆，仕閩為南劍州順昌令，因家順昌。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kui served Min as magistrate of Shunchang in Nanjian Prefecture and settled his family in Shunchang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kui served Min as magistrate of Shunchang in Nanjian Prefecture and settled his family there.

sentences.zh: 特少穎悟，十歲，謁江南李景，獻所為文，景奇之，命作賦，有頃而成，授蘭台校書郎。

translations.literal: Te was precocious as a youth. At the age of ten he called upon Li Jing of Jiangnan, presented writings he had composed, and Jing was amazed. He ordered him to compose a fu, which Te finished in a short while, and appointed him collator of the Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Te was precocious as a youth. At ten he called upon Li Jing of Jiangnan, presented writings he had composed, and Jing was amazed. He ordered him to compose a fu, which Te finished in short order, and appointed him collator of the Orchid Terrace.

sentences.zh: 江南平，偽官皆入見，特袖文以進。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, all the former officials were summoned to audience. Te presented a text he had kept in his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan was pacified, all the former officials were summoned to audience. Te presented a text he had kept in his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 太宗以為長葛尉，改遂州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong appointed him magistrate of Changge and transferred him to recording secretary in Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong appointed him magistrate of Changge and transferred him to recording secretary in Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 代還，命中書引對，授大理寺丞、通判隴州，有治狀。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he was summoned for audience at the Secretariat, appointed vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and made military prefect of Longzhou, where he showed a record of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned, he was summoned for audience at the Secretariat, appointed vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and made military prefect of Longzhou, where he showed a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 田重進鎮永興，太宗以重進武人，選特與楊覃並為通判，人賜白金二百兩，給實奉。

translations.literal: Tian Chongjin was stationed at Yongxing. Emperor Taizong, considering Chongjin a military man, selected Te and Yang Tan together as military prefects. Each was granted two hundred taels of white silver and given a full salary.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chongjin was stationed at Yongxing. Emperor Taizong, considering Chongjin a military man, selected Te and Yang Tan together as military prefects. Each was granted two hundred taels of white silver and given a full salary.

sentences.zh: 會出兵五路討李繼遷，督所部轉芻粟，先期以辦。

translations.literal: When troops were dispatched on five routes to attack Li Jiqian, he supervised the transport of fodder and grain in his jurisdiction and completed the task ahead of schedule.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were dispatched on five routes to attack Li Jiqian, he supervised the transport of fodder and grain in his jurisdiction and completed the task ahead of schedule.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙正辟通判西京留守事。

translations.literal: Lü Mengzheng recruited him as military prefect for the Western Capital garrison administration.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mengzheng recruited him as military prefect for the Western Capital garrison administration.

sentences.zh: 蒙正入相，薦之，入判三司戶部勾院。

translations.literal: When Mengzheng entered the grand council he recommended Te, who was appointed to the Three Departments Revenue Verification Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengzheng entered the grand council he recommended Te, who was appointed to the Three Departments Revenue Verification Office.

sentences.zh: 梁鼎制置陝西青白鹽，前後上議異同，真宗選特與知永興軍張詠同商利害，所奏合旨。

translations.literal: Liang Ding had been commissioner for green-and-white salt in Shaanxi. Memorials on the subject had differed back and forth. Emperor Zhenzong selected Te and Zhang Yong, prefect of Yongxing Circuit, to discuss the pros and cons together. Their report accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ding had been commissioner for green-and-white salt in Shaanxi, and memorials on the subject had differed back and forth. Emperor Zhenzong selected Te and Zhang Yong, prefect of Yongxing Circuit, to discuss the pros and cons together. Their report accorded with the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書祠部員外郎，為戶部副使，詔赴內朝。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Rites, made vice commissioner of the Revenue Office, and ordered to attend the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Rites, made vice commissioner of the Revenue Office, and ordered to attend the inner court.

sentences.zh: 三司副使預內朝，自特始。

translations.literal: Vice commissioners of the Three Departments attending the inner court began with Te.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioners of the Three Departments attending the inner court began with Te.

sentences.zh: 徙鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Office.

sentences.zh: 真宗北征，命同知留司三司公事，遷司封員外郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong marched north, Te was ordered to assist in managing the routine business of the Three Departments left behind at the capital, and was promoted to outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong marched north, Te was ordered to assist in managing the routine business of the Three Departments left behind at the capital, and was promoted to outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 車駕謁陵，為行在三司副使，詔與劉承珪、李溥比較江淮茶法。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the imperial tombs, he served as vice commissioner of the Three Departments on the journey and was ordered, together with Liu Chenggui and Li Pu, to compare the tea laws of the Jianghuai region.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage visited the imperial tombs, he served as vice commissioner of the Three Departments on the journey and was ordered, together with Liu Chenggui and Li Pu, to compare the tea laws of the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 因裁定新製，歲增課百餘萬，特遷祠部郎中。

translations.literal: He thereupon fixed a new system, increasing annual revenue by more than a million, and Te was promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon fixed a new system, increasing annual revenue by more than a million, and Te was promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，祀汾陰，皆為行在三司副使。

translations.literal: For the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai and the sacrifice at Fenyin, he served in each case as vice commissioner of the Three Departments on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: For the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai and the sacrifice at Fenyin, he served in each case as vice commissioner of the Three Departments on the journey.

sentences.zh: 以右諫議大夫權三司使、修玉清昭應宮副使。

translations.literal: As Right Censor-in-Chief he acted as commissioner of the Three Departments and served as deputy commissioner for construction of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace.
translations.idiomatic: As right censor-in-chief he acted as commissioner of the Three Departments and served as deputy commissioner for construction of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace.

sentences.zh: 將祀太清宮，遣特儲供具，為行在三司使。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to sacrifice at the Grand Pure Temple, Te was dispatched to store supplies and served as commissioner of the Three Departments on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to sacrifice at the Grand Pure Temple, Te was dispatched to store supplies and served as commissioner of the Three Departments on the journey.

sentences.zh: 禮成，進給事中，為修景靈宮副使兼修兗州景靈宮、太極觀。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed he was promoted to supervisory censor and made deputy commissioner for construction of the Jingling Palace, with concurrent responsibility for the Jingling Palace and the Grand Ultimate Temple in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed he was promoted to supervisory censor and made deputy commissioner for construction of the Jingling Palace, with concurrent responsibility for the Jingling Palace and the Grand Ultimate Temple in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭應宮成，遷尚書工部侍郎，真拜三司使。

translations.literal: When the Zhaoying Palace was completed he was transferred to vice minister of works and formally appointed commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhaoying Palace was completed he was transferred to vice minister of works and formally appointed commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 樞密使寇準言特奸邪，又數與爭事，帝為出準，特在職如故。

translations.literal: Director of Military Affairs Kou Zhun said that Te was treacherous and corrupt and repeatedly clashed with him over affairs. The emperor removed Zhun for this, and Te remained in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Military Affairs Kou Zhun said that Te was treacherous and corrupt and repeatedly clashed with him over affairs. The emperor removed Zhun for this, and Te remained in office as before.

sentences.zh: 後罷三司，以戶部侍郎同玉清昭應宮副使。

translations.literal: Later he was removed from the Three Departments and made vice minister of revenue with concurrent service as deputy commissioner of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was removed from the Three Departments and made vice minister of revenue with concurrent service as deputy commissioner of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace.

sentences.zh: 兗州宮觀成，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Yanzhou temples and abbeys were completed he was transferred to vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yanzhou temples and abbeys were completed he was transferred to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，為修上《聖祖寶冊》副使，轉尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi he served as deputy commissioner for the presentation of the Precious Register of the Sage Ancestor and was transferred to right vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi he served as deputy commissioner for the presentation of the Precious Register of the Sage Ancestor and was transferred to right vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時天下完富，丁謂以符瑞、土木迎帝意，而以特有心計，使幹財利佐之。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was prosperous and wealthy. Ding Wei used omens and auspicious signs and construction projects to win the emperor's favor, and because Te was shrewd in calculation, employed him to manage finances and assist him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm was prosperous and wealthy. Ding Wei used omens and auspicious signs and construction projects to win the emperor's favor, and because Te was shrewd in calculation, employed him to manage finances and assist him.

sentences.zh: 然特亦天性邪險，善附會，故謂始終善特，當時與陳彭年等號「五鬼」，語在《王欽若傳》。

translations.literal: Yet Te was also by nature treacherous and dangerous and skilled at ingratiating himself, so Ding always treated Te well. At the time he and Chen Pengnian and others were called the "Five Demons," as related in the biography of Wang Qinruo.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Te was also by nature treacherous and dangerous and skilled at ingratiating himself, so Ding always treated Te well. At the time he and Chen Pengnian and others were called the "Five Demons," as related in the biography of Wang Qinruo.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，以工部尚書兼太子賓客，改詹事。

translations.literal: When Renzong was in the Eastern Palace, Te served as minister of works with concurrent appointment as tutor to the crown prince, then was changed to grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was in the Eastern Palace, Te served as minister of works with concurrent appointment as tutor to the crown prince, then was changed to grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 丁謂欲引為樞密副使，而李迪執不可。

translations.literal: Ding Wei wished to bring him in as deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but Li Di firmly objected.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei wished to bring him in as deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but Li Di firmly objected.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，進刑部尚書、翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, Te was promoted to minister of justice and Hanlin academician reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne, Te was promoted to minister of justice and Hanlin academician reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 謂貶，特亦落職知許州。

translations.literal: When Ding was demoted, Te also lost his rank and was made prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding was demoted, Te also lost his rank and was made prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 還朝，以戶部尚書知通進銀台司、判尚書都省、勾當三班院。

translations.literal: Upon returning to court he was made minister of revenue with charge of the Gateway for Memorials and Silver Terrace Office, assigned to the Ministry of Personnel, and put in charge of the Three Classes Office.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning to court he was made minister of revenue with charge of the Gateway for Memorials and Silver Terrace Office, assigned to the Ministry of Personnel, and put in charge of the Three Classes Office.

sentences.zh: 特體素羸，然未嘗一日謁告，及得疾，才五日而卒。

translations.literal: Te's constitution had always been frail, yet he never once took leave for a single day. When he fell ill, he died after only five days.
translations.idiomatic: Te's constitution had always been frail, yet he never once took leave for a single day. When he fell ill, he died after only five days.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as left vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as left vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太后遣中使祀奠。

translations.literal: The empress dowager dispatched a palace envoy to offer sacrifice and libation.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager dispatched a palace envoy to offer sacrifice and libation.

sentences.zh: 特精敏，喜吏職，據案終日不倦。

translations.literal: Te was sharp and keen, delighted in administrative duties, and worked at his desk all day without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Te was sharp and keen, delighted in administrative duties, and worked at his desk all day without tiring.

sentences.zh: 真宗數訪以朝廷大事，特因有所中傷，人以此憚焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong repeatedly consulted him on major affairs of state. Te would use these occasions to slander others, and people therefore feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong repeatedly consulted him on major affairs of state. Te would use these occasions to slander others, and people therefore feared him.

sentences.zh: 奉詔撰《會計錄》三十卷。

translations.literal: By imperial order he compiled the Records of Accounts in thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he compiled the Records of Accounts in thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 又為《東封西祀朝謁太清宮慶賜總例》三十六卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled General Precedents for the Eastern Fengshan, Western Sacrifice, Audience at the Grand Pure Temple, and Celebration Grants in thirty-six volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled General Precedents for the Eastern Fengshan, Western Sacrifice, Audience at the Grand Pure Temple, and Celebration Grants in thirty-six volumes.

sentences.zh: 子濰、洙。

translations.literal: His sons were Wei and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wei and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 濰亦有吏能，曆官至三司鹽鐵副使，以秘書監致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Wei also had administrative ability, rose through office to vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Office, retired as director of the Imperial Library, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei also had administrative ability, rose through office to vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Office, retired as director of the Imperial Library, and died.

sentences.zh: 洙，官至司農卿、知壽州，臨事苛急，鼓角將夜入州廨，拔堂檻鐵鉤擊殺之。

translations.literal: Zhu rose to director of the Directorate of Agriculture and prefect of Shouzhou. He was harsh and impatient in handling affairs. When the watchman was about to enter the prefectural office at night, Zhu pulled an iron hook from the hall railing and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu rose to director of the Directorate of Agriculture and prefect of Shouzhou. He was harsh and impatient in handling affairs. When the watchman was about to enter the prefectural office at night, Zhu pulled an iron hook from the hall railing and beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 丁謂，字謂之，後更字公言，蘇州長洲人。

translations.literal: Ding Wei, styled Weizhi, later changed his style to Gongyan, was a native of Changzhou in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei, courtesy name Weizhi, later changed it to Gongyan, and came from Changzhou in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 少與孫何友善，同袖文謁王禹偁，禹偁大驚重之，以為自唐韓愈、柳宗元後，二百年始有此作。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Sun He. Together they carried writings in their sleeves and called upon Wang Yucheng. Yucheng was greatly astonished and held them in high esteem, saying that since Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan of Tang, two hundred years had passed before such writing appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was friendly with Sun He. Together they carried writings in their sleeves and called upon Wang Yucheng. Yucheng was greatly astonished and held them in high esteem, saying that since Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan of Tang, two hundred years had passed before such writing appeared.

sentences.zh: 世謂之「 孫丁」。

translations.literal: The world called them "Sun and Ding."
translations.idiomatic: The world called them "Sun and Ding."

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，登進士甲科，為大理評事、通判饒州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he passed the jinshi examination in the first rank, was appointed judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, and made military prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua he passed the jinshi examination in the first rank, was appointed judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, and made military prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，直史館，以太子中允為福建路采訪。

translations.literal: After a year he was appointed to the Historiography Institute and sent as investigator of the Fujian Circuit with the rank of palace aide to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was appointed to the Historiography Institute and sent as investigator of the Fujian Circuit with the rank of palace aide to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 還，上茶鹽利害，遂為轉運使，除三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: Upon returning he submitted a report on the pros and cons of tea and salt policy, was made transport commissioner, and appointed judge of the Revenue Office in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning he submitted a report on the pros and cons of tea and salt policy, was made transport commissioner, and appointed judge of the Revenue Office in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 峽路蠻擾邊，命往體量。

translations.literal: When the barbarians of the Gorges Route were harassing the frontier, he was ordered to go and assess the situation.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians of the Gorges Route were harassing the frontier, he was ordered to go and assess the situation.

sentences.zh: 還奏稱旨，領峽路轉運使，累遷尚書工部員外郎，會分川峽為四路，改夔州路。

translations.literal: Upon returning his memorial accorded with the emperor's intent. He was put in charge of the Gorges Route transport commission, was promoted in succession to outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Works, and when Sichuan and the Gorges were divided into four routes, was transferred to the Kuizhou Route.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning his memorial accorded with the emperor's intent. He was put in charge of the Gorges Route transport commission, was promoted in succession to outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Works, and when Sichuan and the Gorges were divided into four routes, was transferred to the Kuizhou Route.

sentences.zh: 初，王均叛，朝廷調施、黔、高、溪州蠻子弟以捍賊，既而反為寇。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Jun rebelled, the court mobilized the young men of the Shi, Qian, Gao, and Xi prefectures among the barbarians to resist the rebels, but they in turn became raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Jun rebelled, the court mobilized the young men of the Shi, Qian, Gao, and Xi prefectures among the barbarians to resist the rebels, but they in turn became raiders.

sentences.zh: 謂至，召其種酋開諭之，且言有詔赦不殺。

translations.literal: When Wei arrived he summoned the chieftains of their tribes and admonished them openly, also saying that there was an edict granting amnesty and forbidding execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei arrived he summoned the chieftains of their tribes and admonished them openly, also saying that there was an edict granting amnesty and forbidding execution.

sentences.zh: 酋感泣，願世奉貢。

translations.literal: The chieftains wept in gratitude and wished to render tribute for generations.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains wept in gratitude and wished to render tribute for generations.

sentences.zh: 乃作誓刻石柱，立境上。

translations.literal: He thereupon had an oath carved on a stone pillar and erected it on the border.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon had an oath carved on a stone pillar and erected it on the border.

sentences.zh: 蠻地饒粟而常乏鹽，謂聽以粟易鹽，蠻人大悅。

translations.literal: The barbarian lands were rich in grain but often lacked salt. Wei permitted them to exchange grain for salt, and the barbarians were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian lands were rich in grain but often lacked salt. Wei permitted them to exchange grain for salt, and the barbarians were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 先時，屯兵施州而饋以夔、萬州粟。

translations.literal: Previously, troops had been stationed at Shizhou and supplied with grain from Kuizhou and Wanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, troops had been stationed at Shizhou and supplied with grain from Kuizhou and Wanzhou.

sentences.zh: 至是，民無轉餉之勞，施之諸砦，積聚皆可給。

translations.literal: At this point the people were spared the labor of transporting provisions. The stockpiles at the various stockades in Shizhou were all sufficient for supply.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the people were spared the labor of transporting provisions. The stockpiles at the various stockades in Shizhou were all sufficient for supply.

sentences.zh: 特遷刑部員外郎，賜白金三百兩。

translations.literal: He was specially promoted to outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Justice and granted three hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to outer-section secretary in the Ministry of Justice and granted three hundred taels of white silver.

sentences.zh: 時溪蠻別種有入寇者，謂遣高、溪酋帥其徒討擊，出兵援之，擒生蠻六百六十，得所掠漢口四百餘人。

translations.literal: At that time certain other tribes among the Xi barbarians were raiding. Wei dispatched the chieftains of Gao and Xi to lead their followers in punitive action, sent troops to support them, captured six hundred and sixty living barbarians, and recovered more than four hundred Han people who had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: At that time certain other tribes among the Xi barbarians were raiding. Wei dispatched the chieftains of Gao and Xi to lead their followers in punitive action, sent troops to support them, captured six hundred and sixty living barbarians, and recovered more than four hundred Han people who had been seized.

sentences.zh: 復上言：黔南蠻族多善馬，請致館，犒給緡帛，歲收市之。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "The barbarian tribes of southern Qian are skilled in raising horses. I request that lodges be established, that they be rewarded with silk and cloth, and that horses be purchased from them annually."
translations.idiomatic: He further memorialized: "The barbarian tribes of southern Qian are skilled in raising horses. I request that lodges be established, that they be rewarded with silk and cloth, and that horses be purchased from them annually."

sentences.zh: 其後徙置夔州城砦，皆謂所經畫也。

translations.literal: The later relocation and establishment of walled stockades in Kuizhou were all plans laid by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The later relocation and establishment of walled stockades in Kuizhou were all plans laid by Wei.

sentences.zh: 居五年，不得代，乃詔舉自代者，於是入權三司鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: After five years in office he had received no replacement. An edict was then issued calling for someone to recommend his own successor, and he entered the capital to act as vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Office.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in office he had received no replacement. An edict was then issued calling for someone to recommend his own successor, and he entered the capital to act as vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢知制誥，判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to drafting secretary for imperial edicts and assigned to the Ministry of Personnel's Board for Selection within the Streams.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to drafting secretary for imperial edicts and assigned to the Ministry of Personnel's Board for Selection within the Streams.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，契丹犯河北，真宗幸澶淵，以謂知鄆州兼齊、濮等州安撫使，提舉轉運兵馬巡檢事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde the Khitan invaded Hebei. Emperor Zhenzong went to Chanyuan and appointed Wei prefect of Yanzhou with concurrent authority as pacification commissioner of Qi, Pu, and other prefectures, with charge over transport, troops, horses, and patrol affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingde the Khitan invaded Hebei. Emperor Zhenzong went to Chanyuan and appointed Wei prefect of Yanzhou with concurrent authority as pacification commissioner of Qi, Pu, and other prefectures, with charge over transport, troops, horses, and patrol affairs.

sentences.zh: 契丹深入，民驚擾，爭趣楊劉渡，而舟人邀利，不時濟。

translations.literal: As the Khitan penetrated deeply, the people were alarmed and disturbed and all rushed toward the Yangliu crossing, but the boatmen sought profit and did not ferry them across in time.
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan penetrated deeply, the people were alarmed and disturbed and all rushed toward the Yangliu crossing, but the boatmen sought profit and did not ferry them across in time.

sentences.zh: 謂取死罪紿為舟人，斬河上，舟人懼，民得悉渡。

translations.literal: Wei took a man condemned to death, disguised him as a boatman, and had him executed on the riverbank. The boatmen were terrified, and the people were all able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took a man condemned to death, disguised him as a boatman, and had him executed on the riverbank. The boatmen were terrified, and the people were all able to cross.

sentences.zh: 遂立部分，使並河執旗幟，擊刁斗，呼聲聞百餘里，契丹遂引去。

translations.literal: He then established formations, had men along the river hold banners and flags, strike clappers, and shout so that the sound carried more than a hundred li, and the Khitan thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then established formations, had men along the river hold banners and flags, strike clappers, and shout so that the sound carried more than a hundred li, and the Khitan thereupon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，召為右諫議大夫、權三司使。

translations.literal: The following year he was summoned as Right Censor-in-Chief and acting commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned as right censor-in-chief and acting commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 上《會計錄》，以景德四年民賦戶口之籍，較咸平六年之數，具上史館，請自今以咸平籍為額，歲較其數以聞，詔獎之。

translations.literal: He submitted the Records of Accounts, comparing the registers of household tax and population for the fourth year of Jingde with the figures for the sixth year of Xianping, and presented the full report to the Historiography Institute. He requested that from now on the Xianping registers serve as the quota, with annual comparison of the figures reported. An edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the Records of Accounts, comparing the registers of household tax and population for the fourth year of Jingde with the figures for the sixth year of Xianping, and presented the full report to the Historiography Institute. He requested that from now on the Xianping registers serve as the quota, with annual comparison of the figures reported. An edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 尋加樞密直學士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was given the additional title of direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was given the additional title of direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，議封禪，未決，帝問以經費，謂對「大計有餘」，議乃決。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong xiangfu, when the Fengshan sacrifice was under discussion but not yet decided, the emperor asked about expenses. Wei replied, "The overall plan has a surplus," and the decision was then made.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhong xiangfu, when the Fengshan sacrifice was under discussion but not yet decided, the emperor asked about expenses. Wei replied, "The overall plan has a surplus," and the decision was then made.

sentences.zh: 因詔謂為計度泰山路糧草使。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon appointed Wei commissioner for calculating grain and fodder on the Mount Tai route.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon appointed Wei commissioner for calculating grain and fodder on the Mount Tai route.

sentences.zh: 初，議即宮城乾地營玉清昭應宮，左右有諫者。

translations.literal: At first, when it was proposed to build the Yujing Zhaoying Palace on dry ground within the palace city, there were advisers on both sides who remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when it was proposed to build the Yujing Zhaoying Palace on dry ground within the palace city, there were advisers on both sides who remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 帝召問，謂對曰：「陛下有天下之富，建一宮奉上帝，且所以祈皇嗣也。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for questioning. Wei replied: "Your Majesty possesses the wealth of the realm. To build one palace to serve the Supreme Lord is also a means of praying for an imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him for questioning. Wei replied: "Your Majesty possesses the wealth of the realm. To build one palace to serve the Supreme Lord is also a means of praying for an imperial heir.

sentences.zh: 群臣有沮陛下者，願以此論之。」

translations.literal: If any among the ministers obstruct Your Majesty, I hope this argument may be used against them."
translations.idiomatic: If any among the ministers obstruct Your Majesty, I hope this argument may be used against them."

sentences.zh: 王旦密疏諫，帝如謂所對告之，旦不復敢言。

translations.literal: Wang Dan submitted a secret memorial remonstrating, but the emperor told him what Wei had answered, and Dan no longer dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan submitted a secret memorial remonstrating, but the emperor told him what Wei had answered, and Dan no longer dared speak.

sentences.zh: 乃以謂為修玉清昭應宮使，復為天書扶侍使，遷給事中，真拜三司使。

translations.literal: Wei was then made commissioner for construction of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace, again served as attendant for the Heavenly Writ, was promoted to supervisory censor, and formally appointed commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was then made commissioner for construction of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace, again served as attendant for the Heavenly Writ, was promoted to supervisory censor, and formally appointed commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，為行在三司使。

translations.literal: For the sacrifice at Fenyin he served as commissioner of the Three Departments on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: For the sacrifice at Fenyin he served as commissioner of the Three Departments on the journey.

sentences.zh: 建會靈觀，謂復總領之。

translations.literal: When the Huiling Temple was built, Wei again took overall charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huiling Temple was built, Wei again took overall charge of it.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書禮部侍郎，進戶部，參知政事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of rites, advanced to the Ministry of Revenue, and made participant in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of rites, advanced to the Ministry of Revenue, and made vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 建安軍鑄玉皇像，為迎奉使。

translations.literal: When Jian'an Circuit cast an image of the Jade Emperor, he served as commissioner for receiving and escorting it.
